# Lipsync Papers

> Papers related to lipsync.: research papers converted to Markdown so that people and LLMs can read them straight from this repository.

## Finding a paper

- [Title index](index/README.md): one file per publication year, one line per paper with its date, title and a link to its Markdown. Start here.
- [papers.csv](papers.csv): every paper with its identifier, title, abstract, authors, publication date, URL, source, DOI, arXiv ID and categories, oldest first. It is large; search it rather than reading it whole.
- [README.md](README.md): the 30 most recent papers.

## Reading a paper

- Each paper is one file, `papers/<name>.md`, where `<name>` is the paper's identifier as a slug plus a short hash, for example `papers/arxiv-2111-05095v1--62e4caaf9baf.md`.
- Every file starts with YAML front matter: `identifier`, `title`, `authors`, `published`, `url`, `source`, `doi`, `arxiv_id` and `categories`.
- Figures are stored next to the paper in `papers/<name>.figures/` and linked with relative paths.
- Math is LaTeX. Papers converted from arXiv HTML have inline math as ``$`...`$`` and display equations in `math` code blocks. Papers converted from PDF have display equations as `$$...$$`, or `<!-- formula-not-decoded -->` where an equation was not recognized, and their inline math is plain text.
- `papers/<name>.fixme.txt` means the paper could not be converted; the file holds the error. Such papers, and papers still waiting to be converted, link to their source URL in the title index.
